The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[8\operatorname{arcsin}⁡({e}^{x})] \\  & =8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{({e}^{x})}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1-{e}^{2x}}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{8{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{1-{e}^{2x}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{4}-\frac{1}{4x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5+9\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x) \\  & =0+9\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x) \\  & =0+9\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(2x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{arcsin}^{5}⁡(4x)] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(4x)] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot [\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(4x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x)] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot [\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(4x)^{2}}}\cdot 4] \\  & =5{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)\cdot \frac{4}{\sqrt{1-16{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{20{arcsin}^{4}⁡(4x)}{\sqrt{1-16{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{4}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x+4\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =5+4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =5+4(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =5-\frac{4}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-5\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =2-5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =2-5(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =2+\frac{5}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(15\operatorname{arccos}⁡x+8x) \\  & =15\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)+8 \\  & =15(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})+8 \\  & =8-\frac{15}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-2\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =0-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =-2(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5x-4)+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(5x-4)}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x-4)+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(5x-4)}^{2}}\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{5}{1+{(5x-4)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({arctan}^{2}⁡(3{e}^{x})) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{1}{1+{(3{e}^{x})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x}) \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{1}{1+9{e}^{2x}}\cdot 3{e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{6{e}^{x}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{e}^{x})}{1+9{e}^{2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[3\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{2}-2x)] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{1+({x}^{2}-2x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-2x) \\  & =\frac{3}{1+{x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}}\cdot (2x-2) \\  & =\frac{6x-6}{{x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={f}^{′}(2) \\  & =\frac{6(2)-6}{(2)^{4}-4(2)^{3}+4(2)^{2}+1} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2{x}^{3}+x)] \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(2{x}^{3}+x)}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}+x) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(2{x}^{3}+x)^{2}}\cdot (6{x}^{2}+1) \\  & =\frac{6{x}^{2}+1}{1+(2{x}^{3}+x)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5{x}^{3})] \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(5{x}^{3})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+25{x}^{6}}\cdot 15{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{15{x}^{2}}{1+25{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{{x}^{6}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3}))-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{6}+1)}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{6}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 6{x}^{5}}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{({x}^{6}+1)(3{x}^{2})}{{x}^{6}+1}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arcsin x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(3{x}^{2})) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(3{x}^{2})^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{1-9{x}^{4}}}\cdot (6x) \\  & =\frac{30x}{\sqrt{1-9{x}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arccos x) = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-8x)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5-8x)^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-8x) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(25-80x+64{x}^{2})}}\cdot (-8) \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{80x-24-64{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{4(20x-6-16{x}^{2})}} \\  & =\frac{8}{2\sqrt{20x-6-16{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{20x-6-16{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arctan x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-7x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(-7x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7x) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+49{x}^{2}}\cdot (-7) \\  & =-\frac{7}{1+49{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the product rule and using the formula for the derivative of $\arccos x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) & =x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
